{"user_request": "Create a compact, self-contained QA training case from the June 12 Q2 board-evidence source-completeness packet. Show that source completeness and claim readiness are separate judgments, identify the sections that passed source-completeness review, explain the maturity-dependent exception including its cohort type and size and available leading read, and state the limits of what the packet decided. Title the document `Board-source QA case — Q2 source completeness vs claim readiness`.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Board-source QA case — Q2 source completeness vs claim readiness", "body": "QA training case

Source: June 12 Q2 board-evidence source-completeness packet

Scenario
The packet reviewed four evidence sections independently. A section could have complete source documentation without being ready for a board claim. The QA task is to preserve that distinction and avoid treating a complete packet as claim approval.

What passed source-completeness review
These three preparation sections had all required source fields present:

- Expansion Assist
- Pricing-page path quality
- CS auto-nudge

For each, the packet documented the required source owner, denominator or exact coverage fields, measurement limits, exclusions, and locations for reliability evidence. No required source field was missing in these sections.

Maturity-dependent exception: Helio Start
Helio Start was the exception. The packet recorded a fixed 50-workspace paid cohort and a complete leading read: 39 of 50 workspaces reached first integration by day 7. That is an available early operating signal, not a mature customer-outcome result.

The mature customer-outcome row remained incomplete because all 50 workspaces did not yet have complete day-90 windows. Therefore, the packet could not treat paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, or account-level support effort as mature outcomes. The missing maturity window is a claim-readiness limitation, not evidence that the early read was absent.

Two judgments to keep separate

1. Source completeness: Are the required source fields, ownership, coverage or denominator, definitions, limits, exclusions, and reliability-evidence locations present and documented?

2. Claim readiness: Is the evidence sufficiently mature and appropriately bounded for the proposed claim? This requires more than populated source fields; it depends on complete outcome windows, valid interpretation, and the applicable limits on causal, revenue, forecast, and board use.

A section may pass source-completeness review and still require a separate claim-readiness decision. Conversely, an early result can be fully recorded while remaining insufficient for a mature claim.

What the June 12 packet decided—and did not decide

It documented source-complete preparation for Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and CS auto-nudge, and it recorded Helio Start’s fixed denominator and leading day-7 read while flagging the incomplete mature-outcome row.

It did not make a claim, close a lane, approve board readiness, or authorize causal, revenue, or forecast treatment. It also did not convert the Helio Start day-7 result into a mature customer, acquisition, revenue, or forecast claim. Any later claim or board-use decision required a separate review under the relevant evidence and authority boundaries.

QA answer key

- “All four sections are board-ready because the packet is complete.” Incorrect. Source completeness and claim readiness are separate judgments.
- “Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and CS auto-nudge passed source-completeness review.” Correct.
- “Helio Start had no usable evidence.” Incorrect. It had a fixed 50-workspace paid cohort and a 39-of-50 day-7 first-integration read.
- “Helio Start had a mature outcome.” Incorrect. Complete day-90 windows for all 50 workspaces were not yet available.
- “The packet approved a board claim.” Incorrect. It made no claim, closed no lane, and made no board-readiness decision.

QA rule of thumb
Record what is complete, identify what is maturity-dependent, preserve the leading read without overstating it, and never infer claim approval from source completeness alone."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_134_02", "path": "args", "criterion": "The document identifies Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and CS auto-nudge as the three source-complete sections, and conveys that each had its required source owner, denominator or exact coverage fields, measurement limits, exclusions, and reliability-evidence location, with no required source field missing. Missing any section or materially misstating why it was source-complete must fail.

The document states that Helio Start had a fixed paid cohort of exactly 50 workspaces and a complete leading read of exactly 39 of 50 reaching first integration by day 7, while its mature customer-outcome row remained incomplete because all 50 did not yet have complete day-90 windows. It must not portray the day-7 result as a mature outcome.

The document clearly teaches that source completeness and claim or board readiness are separate judgments, and states that the June 12 packet itself made no claim, closed no lane, and made no board-readiness decision. Any assertion that the packet approved a claim, closed a lane, or declared board readiness must fail.", "value": {"title": "Board-source QA case — Q2 source completeness vs claim readiness", "body": "QA training case

Source: June 12 Q2 board-evidence source-completeness packet

What passed source-completeness review
These three preparation sections had all required source fields present:

- Expansion Assist
- Pricing-page path quality
- CS auto-nudge

For each, the packet documented the required source owner, denominator or exact coverage fields, measurement limits, exclusions, and locations for reliability evidence. No required source field was missing in these sections.

Maturity-dependent exception: Helio Start
Helio Start was the exception. The packet recorded a fixed 50-workspace paid cohort and a complete leading read: 39 of 50 workspaces reached first integration by day 7. That is an available early operating signal, not a mature customer-outcome result.

The mature customer-outcome row remained incomplete because all 50 workspaces did not yet have complete day-90 windows. Therefore, the packet could not treat paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, or account-level support effort as mature outcomes. The missing maturity window is a claim-readiness limitation, not evidence that the early read was absent.

Two judgments to keep separate

1. Source completeness: Are the required source fields, ownership, coverage or denominator, definitions, limits, exclusions, and reliability-evidence locations present and documented?

2. Claim readiness: Is the evidence sufficiently mature and appropriately bounded for the proposed claim? This requires more than populated source fields; it depends on complete outcome windows, valid interpretation, and the applicable limits on causal, revenue, forecast, and board use.

A section may pass source-completeness review and still require a separate claim-readiness decision. Conversely, an early result can be fully recorded while remaining insufficient for a mature claim.

It documented source-complete preparation for Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and CS auto-nudge, and it recorded Helio Start’s fixed denominator and leading day-7 read while flagging the incomplete mature-outcome row.

It did not make a claim, close a lane, approve board readiness, or authorize causal, revenue, or forecast treatment. Any later claim or board-use decision required a separate review under the relevant evidence and authority boundaries.

QA answer key

- “All four sections are board-ready because the packet is complete.” Incorrect. Source completeness and claim readiness are separate judgments.
- “Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and CS auto-nudge passed source-completeness review.” Correct.
- “Helio Start had no usable evidence.” Incorrect. It had a fixed 50-workspace paid cohort and a 39-of-50 day-7 first-integration read.
- “Helio Start had a mature outcome.” Incorrect. Complete day-90 windows for all 50 workspaces were not yet available.
- “The packet approved a board claim.” Incorrect. It made no claim, closed no lane, and made no board-readiness decision.
